rounds.text: Zodiac Ventures Ltd trades at a remarkably low valuation, sitting at a price-to-earnings ratio of 4.93x against a sector benchmark of 18.61x, and a price-to-book ratio of just 0.20x compared to a sector benchmark of 1.33x [E1, E2, E6, E7]. The underlying business is experiencing a powerful operational acceleration, evidenced by compounded sales growth of 242% and profit growth of 63% over the trailing twelve months [E17, E21], heavily outperforming the broader sector medians [E65, E66]. Furthermore, a discounted cash flow model suggests an intrinsic value of Rs 9 per share against a market price of Rs 1.05, offering a substantial margin of safety of 87.9% [E42, E43]. The reverse DCF indicates that the current price pessimistically assumes a -12.4% earnings growth, while the company operates within a supportive services sector tailwind score of +0.64 [E44, E64]. Conceded: promoter holding has dropped significantly to 29.37% from 64.33% over recent years, and operating cash flow for March 2026 was negative at Rs -18.63 Cr [E34, E40].

Zodiac Ventures exhibits severe operational instability, evidenced by a massive collapse in operating margins from 220% three years ago to just 20% in the trailing twelve months [E29]. This downward trend is further confirmed by the yearly operating-margin trajectory, which has been consistently decreasing over the last four years [E31]. The company’s ability to generate actual cash is deeply concerning, as operating cash flow was negative Rs 18.63 Cr in March 2026, leading to a disastrous cash conversion ratio of -12.10x [E33, E34]. Compounding these operational failures, promoter confidence appears to be eroding, with holdings plummeting from 64.33% in December 2023 to just 29.37% as of September 2026 [E40]. Furthermore, the company’s reliance on non-core activities is highlighted by the inclusion of Rs 2.40 Cr in other income within its earnings [E54]. Conceded: the company trades at a low P/E of 4.93x and a P/B of 0.20x, suggesting the market has already priced in significant distress [E1, E2].

Conceded: operating margins dropped over the trailing twelve months and the yearly operating-margin trend reads decreasing [E29, E31]. However, dismissing the business on those margins ignores an overwhelming top-line surge, with trailing twelve-month sales compounding at 242% and recent quarterly sales growth flagged at over 600% [E17, E57]. While operating cash flow for March 2026 was negative [E34], the company trades at a deeply discounted price-to-book ratio of 0.20x against a book value of ₹ 5.38 and a P/E of just 4.93x [E1, E2], offering an intrinsic value estimate of ₹ 9 per share [E42]. The bear highlights other income [E54], but net profit still grew 63% over the trailing twelve months and 128% year-over-year [E21, E59], demonstrating that core profitability and fundamentals are dramatically outpacing the depressed share price [E45]. Finally, while promoter holdings have decreased [E40], the company operates within a supportive services sector tailwind score of +0.64 [E64] and is fundamentally outperforming expectations during this turnaround [E46, E63].

Conceded: trailing twelve-month sales compounded at 242% and recent quarterly sales growth was flagged at over 600% [E17, E57]. However, that explosive top-line acceleration is completely disconnected from efficiency, as operating margins collapsed by 201 percentage points in the TTM period and have trended downward for four straight years [E29, E31]. The bull leans heavily on a cheap valuation of 0.20x book value and a P/E of 4.93x [E1, E2], but ignores that this low multiple coincides with a cratering share price sitting at just 5% of its 52-week range and down 53% over the past year [E5, E24]. Furthermore, the reported net profit growth of 63% TTM and 128% year-over-year [E21, E59] is severely compromised by the inclusion of Rs. 2.40 Cr in other income [E54], masking deteriorating underlying operations. Conceded: the services sector carries a positive tailwind score [E64]. Yet this macro backdrop has failed to prevent operating cash flow and free cash flow from plunging into massive negative territory at Rs -18.63 Cr and Rs -18.69 Cr respectively in March 2026 [E34, E35], driving cash conversion to a disastrous -12.10x [E33]. Finally, insiders are signaling a lack of confidence as promoters slashed their stake by nearly 35 percentage points down to 29.37% [E40].
